Cost decision

The generalized pair-frame law is conceptual, not a physical m-by-p-squared matrix. For a dense local k-by-k metric, each location has k squared metric entries and local factorization is cubic in k. The compiler therefore budgets actual sum nnz(K_x), sum k_x squared, and sum k_x cubed, selects the additive collapse only for feature-additive metrics, and otherwise streams one support/query at a time.
